2607.13303.title: Faithful Autoformalization of Natural Language Assertions
2607.13303.paper_summary: Formal contracts are essential for software testing and verification, yet writing them remains labor-intensive and error-prone. LLMs offer a promising path toward autoformalization: synthesizing executable assertions from natural-language specifications and thereby bridging the gap between informal developer intent and formal executable specifications. We present Monty: an autoformalization framework for assertions that tackles the challenges of expectations of validity of assertions and ambiguity in natural-language. Our techniques are based on filtering formalizations using a novel conformance score metric and validity scores obtained from testing the code against formalized assertions. We evaluate our approach on 541 assertion-generation tasks derived from 22 collection-like Java classes, and show that our technique produces the ground truth more reliably (improving upto 20 points in precision on average) than when using LLMs naively to translate assertions.
2607.13303.paper_summary_zh: 正式合約對於軟體測試和驗證至關重要，但撰寫這些合約仍然是勞動密集且容易出錯的。LLMs 提供了一條有希望的自動形式化路徑：從自然語言規範中合成可執行的斷言，從而縮短非正式開發者意圖與正式可執行規範之間的鴻溝。我們提出了 Monty：一個針對斷言的自動形式化框架，解決了斷言有效性期望和自然語言歧義的挑戰。我們的技術基於使用新穎的符合度分數指標和從測試代碼對照正式化斷言獲得的有效性分數來過濾形式化。我們在從 22 個類似集合的 Java 類中衍生的 541 個斷言生成任務上評估我們的方法，並顯示我們的技術在產生真實值方面比單純使用 LLMs 翻譯斷言更可靠（平均提高了 20 個精確度點）。
